query: Consider the following context: Non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are promising candidates for low-dimensional magnetocaloric applications. In that context, which method can be used for tuning the magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Tuning the magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys (HEAs) can be achieved through compositional modification, specifically by adjusting the ratio of ferromagnetic to paramagnetic elements.
generation.material_initial_state: Non-equiatomic high-entropy alloy in a disordered face-centered cubic (FCC) structure
generation.intervention: Compositional modification by adjusting the ratio of ferromagnetic (e.g., Fe, Co) to paramagnetic (e.g., Ti, V) elements
generation.conditions: Alloy preparation via arc melting and subsequent annealing at 1000°C for 24 hours
generation.structural_mediator: Atomic-scale mixing and resulting changes in magnetic exchange interactions
generation.mechanism: Modification of magnetic exchange interactions and resulting changes in magnetic ordering and phase transitions
generation.predicted_outcome: A 20% increase in the magnetocaloric effect (ΔS) relative to the baseline alloy composition, measured in units of J/kg·K
generation.baseline: Non-equiatomic HEA with a fixed composition (e.g., Fe40Co30Ni15Cr10Ti5)
generation.boundary: Compositional modifications within the bounds of 20% variation in ferromagnetic to paramagnetic element ratio
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the precise role of individual elements on magnetic behavior and potential interactions with other microstructural features

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of non-equiatomic HEA samples with varying ferromagnetic to paramagnetic element ratios, measure the magnetocaloric effect (ΔS) using magnetization and heat capacity measurements
measurements: Magnetization (M) vs. temperature (T) and magnetic field (H)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured ΔS values do not exceed 10% increase relative to the baseline alloy composition for any of the compositional modifications, the hypothesis is falsified
